caption: The drawing is a technical design rendered in fine black lines on a beige or light tan background, showing two orthographic projections of a wooden settee. The left side features the front view, displaying the settee's overall rectangular form with six turned balusters (vertical spindles) along the upper backrest, three spindle legs in the front (the outermost and one central), and a decorative spindle stretcher running horizontally between the legs. The right side presents the side view, showing the settee’s profile with a curved armrest, three additional turned balusters below the armrest, and the seat extending straight back to a vertical rear support. Multiple horizontal and vertical measurements are marked, with specific dimensions such as height, width, and the spacing of structural elements detailed with tick marks and numerals along the margins. The top of the page contains hand-drawn text “SETTEE 1/100,” “BROOKLYN MUSEUM,” “SCALE ½ = 1 FOOT,” and “ROBERT BRIGADIER.” The drawing is labeled at the bottom as “FRONT VIEW” and “SIDE VIEW.” The overall style is precise and functional, typical of architectural or carpentry blueprints.
title: Settee
